I. From the birth of Savanarola to his becoming a monk. (1452 - 1475)
II. From his entering the cloister to his first arrival in Florence. (1475 - 1481)
III. Lorenzo the Magnificent and the Florentines of his day
IV. Marsilio Ficino and the Platonic Academy
V. His first residence in Tuscany, travels in Lombardy, and return to Florence. (1481 - 1490)
VII. Savonarola's first religious pamphlets and his interpretations of the Scriptures
VIII. Savonarola preaches on the Gospels in the Cathedral He shows his aversion to Lorenzo the Magnificent. He preaches on the First Epistle of St. John (1491)

IX. Death of Lorenzo de' Medici and of Pope Innocent VIII. Election of Alexander VI. Savonarola's journey to Bologna. Separation of the Convent of St. Mark from the Lombard Congregation. Reforms in the Convent. (1492 - 1493)
X. Savonarola expounds the chief points of his doctrines during Advent, 1493. He predicts the coming of the French during the Lent of 1494. (1493 - 1494)
BOOK II. I. 1494. The Coming of the French into Italy
II. November 1494. The Medici are expelled from Florence. Savonarola is sent on an embassy to the French camp
III. November 1494. The revolt of Pisa.The entry of Charles VIII. into Florence; his treaty writh the republic, and his departure.
IV. December 1494. Political condition of Florence, after the departure of the French. Savonarola proposes a new form of government.
V. 1494-1495. Constitution of the new government through Savonarola's efforts.
VI. Savonarola's prophecies and prophetical writings
VII. 1495. Various factions are formed in Florence.
BOOK III. I. 1495-I496. Charles VIII returns to France.
II. 1495-1496. The Pope issues a brief summoning Savonarola to Rome.
III. Savonarola returns to the pulpit as Lenten Preacher in 1496
IV. 1496. Various writings concerning the works of Savonarola.
V. 1496. The straits of the Republic and the disastrous course of the Pisan War.
VI. 1497. Francesco Valori is made Gonfalonier, and proposes several new laws.
BOOK IV. I. 1497. Savonarola's sermons on Ezekiel during Lent
II. 1497. Savonarolas Seron on Ascension Day, and the popular riot.
III. 1497. The arrest of Lamberto dell'Antella.
IV. Savonarola's minor works, both published and unpublished. His "Triumph of the Cross"
V. 1497-1498. Savonarola resumes his sermons on Septaugesima Sunday.
VI. MARCH, 1498. Colloguy of the Florentine Ambassador with the Pope.
VII. April 7, 1498. The ordeal by fire.
VIII. April 8, 9, 1498. The attack and defence of the convent
IX. April 9-25, 1498. Savonarola is examined and put to the question.
X. April 26-May 18, 1498. Fra Domenico, Fra Silvestro, and many other friars and friends of the convent are brought to trial.
XI. May 19-23, 1498. Savonarola is put to fresh torture by the Apostolic Commissioners.
